englishSummary.headline: QoS guidance clarifies DSCP marking options
englishSummary.summary: The page now identifies recommended DSCP values, explains that Windows clients support full DSCP customization, and notes that the listed markings are suggestions. It also points to step-by-step Windows configuration guidance.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators can use the suggested Windows markings or select other traffic markings when required; Mac and mobile client markings remain nonconfigurable.

+#### How the SIP OPTIONS process works
+
+- The SBC sends a TLS connection request that includes a TLS certificate to the SIP proxy server Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) (for example, **sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com**).
+- The SIP proxy checks the connection request.
+    - If the request is valid, the TLS connection is established, and the SBC can use it to send SIP OPTIONS requests to the SIP proxy.
+    - If the request is not valid, the TLS connection is closed and the SIP proxy does not receive SIP OPTIONS requests from the SBC.
+- After it receives a SIP OPTIONS request, the SIP proxy checks the Record-Route header to determine whether the SBC FQDN belongs to a known tenant. If the Record-Route header is not present, the SIP proxy checks the Contact header.
+- If the SBC FQDN is detected and recognized, the SIP proxy sends a SIP 200 OK response by using the same TLS connection.
+- The SIP proxy sends a SIP OPTIONS request to the SBC FQDN that is listed in the Contact header of the SIP OPTIONS request received from the SBC.
+- After receiving a SIP OPTIONS request from the SIP proxy, the SBC responds by sending a SIP 200 OK response. This step confirms that the SBC is healthy.
+- As the final step, the SBC is marked as Active in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
+
+Important
+
+SBC health status shown in Teams admin center is determined by successful SIP OPTIONS exchanges, not by successful call traffic. Therefore, calls might continue to work even when the SBC is shown as Inactive or displays SIP OPTIONS warnings.
+
+Note
+
+In a [hosted model](direct-routing-sbc-multiple-tenants), SIP OPTIONS requests should be sent from only the main (physical) SBC. The status of derived (customer) SBCs is based on the main SBC.
+
+#### Incoming call - tenant and user lookup
+
 On an incoming call, the SIP proxy needs to find the tenant to which the call is destined and find the specific user within this tenant. The tenant administrator might configure non-DID numbers, for example +1001, in multiple tenants. Therefore, it's important to find the specific tenant on which to perform the number lookup because the non-DID numbers might be the same in multiple Microsoft 365 or Office 365 organizations.
 
 This section describes how the SIP proxy finds the tenant and the user, and performs authentication of the SBC on the incoming connection.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Enhanced channel meeting experience
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will enhance channel meetings, allowing scheduling from Teams calendar and Outlook, easier discovery for channel members, and delegate scheduling. Rollout starts November 2026, completing by September 2027 across environments. No admin action needed; informing users is recommended. No compliance issues identified.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 12, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

Microsoft Teams is introducing enhancements for channel meetings to make it easier to schedule meetings in the right context and help teams discover relevant meetings across their channels.

Users will be able to create channel meetings directly from the Teams calendar and create and manage channel meetings from classic Outlook for Windows. Channel members will be able to more easily discover meetings associated with their channels, helping teams stay informed about upcoming discussions and participate in relevant conversations. Administrative assistants and delegates will also be able to schedule channel meetings on behalf of others while keeping meetings connected to the appropriate team and channel.

Rollout Schedule:

Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expect to complete by late November 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late January 2027 (previously mid-December 2026) and expect to complete by late January 2027.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late July 2027.

General Availability (GCC High): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late August 2027.

General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

Users will have additional ways to create, manage, and discover channel meetings in Teams and classic Outlook for Windows. This can help meetings stay connected to the relevant team and channel context.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No admin action is required. You may want to inform users, meeting organizers, administrative assistants, and delegates about the enhanced channel meeting experience.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps in meetings
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams introduces Facilitator, an AI feature that detects and resolves knowledge gaps in meetings by providing relevant answers via web search in the chat. Available from February 2027, it requires Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) and must be manually enabled. Admin controls and user opt-out are supported.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 12, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why

We are introducing a new Microsoft Teams Facilitator capability that proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps during meetings. Facilitator can identify when participants ask questions or express uncertainty and retrieve and share relevant answers using web search in the meeting chat. This enhancement helps improve meeting productivity by reducing interruptions and enabling teams to stay focused on goals while accessing needed information. If a participant asks a factual question and no one responds, Facilitator can provide an answer directly in the meeting chat.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558341.

Rollout Schedule

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early February 2027 (previously early December) and expected to complete mid-February 2027 (previously mid-December)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-February 2027 (previously mid-December) and expected to complete early March 2027 (previously mid-January)

Impact on Your Organization

Who is affected

  • Users in Microsoft Teams meetings where Facilitator is enabled with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams (meetings)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Facilitator will monitor meeting conversations in real time to detect implicit or explicit information needs.
  • When a knowledge gap is identified, Facilitator performs a web search and posts a response in the meeting chat: 
  • Responses are infrequent in practice and typically occur less than once per meeting.
  • Responses are limited to questions relevant to the meeting discussion based on agenda signals and conversational context.
  • Facilitator must be manually added to the meeting and is not enabled by default.
  • A user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license must enable Facilitator for the meeting. Other participants do not need to be licensed to receive responses.
  • Admins can disable Facilitator at the tenant level. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting. If web search is disabled, responses are not generated.
  • Users can stop the behavior at any time by removing Facilitator from the meeting.
  • The feature is supported in standard Teams meetings only and not supported in calls, webinars, or town halls.
  • The experience is supported in meetings that include external or cross-tenant participants.

Action Required/Recommendations

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review your organization’s Copilot web search and Facilitator configuration settings to confirm alignment with your policies.
  • Inform helpdesk and users about proactive Facilitator responses in meeting chats.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you reference Teams meeting experiences.

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (for example, meeting conversations)?Yes. The feature processes meeting conversations in real time to detect knowledge gaps and generate responses.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Facilitator uses AI to interpret meeting content and generate contextual responses during meetings.
Does the change provide end users with a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users receive proactive, AI-generated responses within the Teams meeting chat without needing to prompt the system.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through configuration settings?Yes. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting, which admins can enable or disable to control functionality.
Does the change allow a user to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. Users can stop the behavior by removing Facilitator from the meeting.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Updated recording and transcript access setting behavior for town halls and webinars
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams is updating the "Who has access to the recording or transcript" option for Events App town halls and webinars. It will depend on the RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar settings instead of AllowCloudRecording. The change rolls out worldwide in early to mid-November 2026 with no action required.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We are updating how the Who has access to the recording or transcript option appears for Microsoft Teams Events scheduling through the Events App including town halls and webinars. Currently, when AllowCloudRecording is set to false, this option does not appear for these events. After this change, the option will appear only when the applicable RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar setting in CsTeamsEventsPolicy is enabled.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in early-November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams organizers of Events created via the Events App including town halls and webinars

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft TeamsEvents created via the Events App including town halls and webinars

What will happen

The Who has access to the recording or transcript option will be based on the applicable RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar setting. It will no longer be based on the AllowCloudRecording setting.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required to enable this change.

We recommend updating your internal documentation to reflect this change.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
